items.title: Extent of Crime Stoppers data breach unknown: Sault Police chief
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>James Hopkin reports: The Sault’s police chief says it’s currently unclear how many anonymous tips received by Crime Stoppers locally were potentially exposed in a massive data breach. Both the Sault Ste. Marie Police Service and the Anishinabek Police Service have paused their relationship with the local Crime Stoppers chapter — causing the organization to...</article>

items.title: UNM Health addresses cyberattack in New Mexico after ransomware group claims responsibility
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>John Rupolo reports: University of New Mexico Health is addressing concerns after a cyberattack on Monday, with reports surfacing this week that a ransomware group claimed responsibility for the incident. “So what I can say is we’re also aware of those claims by that group,” said Chris Ramirez, communications director for UNMH. The community’s top...</article>

items.title: Florida education department says data breach may affect 4.9 million people
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Eric Weiss reports: The Florida Department of Education says a breach of its student financial aid website may have exposed personal information, including Social Security numbers, belonging to approximately 4.9 million people. The department said staff learned of unauthorized criminal access to the Florida Student Financial Aid website on Oct. 19. It activated cybersecurity response...</article>

items.title: A RIZAP Employee Uploaded 726 People’s Health Records to a Personal AI Chat
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Rowan Sterling reports: On 20 August 2026 an employee of RIZAP Inc., the Japanese fitness and health-guidance group, was pulling records out of the health-guidance management system it operates for insurers when the data went into a generative AI service on a personal account the company had never approved. The records covered 726 members of...</article>

items.title: Australia severs criminal access to 180,000 computers after breaching Amadey malware backend
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Lukas Brandt writes: Criminals using the Amadey malware lost control of about 180,000 infected computers after operators from the Australian Signals Directorate (ASD) gained access to the operation’s backend and severed the connection between the controllers and the victims. “The next steps that we took were to disconnect that Amadey controller from all those victims,”...</article>

items.title: Student SSNs and Medicaid IDs Exposed in Frontline School Software Breach
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Kalleigh Lane reports: If your school district used Frontline Central or School Health Management, your Social Security number, date of birth, or government ID could have been caught up in a cybersecurity incident. That risk applies to some adults and minors whose information was processed through those products. Frontline Education announced Oct. 26, 2026, that...</article>

items.title: DHS personnel leak exposes contact details and sensitive job information
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>David DiMolfetta reports: Searchable records identifying more than 41,000 current and former Department of Homeland Security employees and contractors were published Wednesday, exposing contact information and details about sensitive assignments across the department, according to the organizations behind the release. The transparency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets — known as DDoSecrets — said it received...</article>

items.title: JPN: Times Car reporting ¥5.5 billion loss has firms bracing for data breach fallout
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Maddie Baker and Spencer Landers As cyberattacks continue across Japan, companies are coming to realize the great financial risk of such attacks if their lax cybersecurity systems cause millions of peoples’ personal information to be leaked. Times Car, which saw personal data that included the driver’s licenses of 1.46 million people leaked in September, is learning...</article>

items.title: KR: Bithumb discloses data leak after internal system breach; One of three financial firm breaches reported that day
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>CoinTelegraph reports: South Korea’s crypto exchange Bithumb is investigating the extent of a data leak caused by a hack of its internal mobile system earlier this week, Yonhap News Agency reported Wednesday. Bithumb discovered the breach of its in-house mobile system — the platform used by employees to communicate internally — on Tuesday and notified...</article>

items.title: Japanese internet giant GMO tells customers to shut down and disconnect PCs from the internet following data breach and ransomware threat
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Sead Fadilpašić reports: Japanese internet giant GMO Group has told its customers to scan their computers for viruses, back up all of their data, disconnect the devices from the internet and then shut them down. The announcement, which literally told customers, “unplug any cords connected to your PC,” was made in response to a cyberattack...</article>

items.title: AU: Northern Territory Health backtracks on claim only five patients impacted by RDH privacy breach
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Grace Atta reports: The Northern Territory health department has backtracked on its claim that only five patients were affected by a privacy breach that led to pregnant women’s confidential medical information being shared with 28,000 followers on Instagram by a “medical observer”. The admission comes after the ABC earlier this week contacted multiple women it...</article>

items.title: Traceability becomes the new battleground in healthcare data breach litigation
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Abbye Alexander, Esq., Henry Norwood, Esq., and Emily Taing, Esq. of Kaufman Dolowich LLP write: Recent caselaw suggests a shift in how courts analyze healthcare data breach claims.
